newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China Merchants Holdings sets $200 mln funding.
newsitem.headline: China Merchants Holdings sets $200 mln funding.

text.p: China Merchant Holding Co Ltd's US$200 million financing facility has been launched into general syndication via a special purpose company, bankers said on Friday.
The borrowing amount has been increased to US$200 million from US$100 million due to oversubscription in the underwriting phase, they said.
The facility is guaranteed by China Merchant Holding Co Ltd.
It has a final maturity of five years. The first three years is a U.S. commercial paper programme combined with a revolving credit facility and the remaining two years will be a term loan facility.
Therefore, the first three years of the facility could be on an unfunded basis to the syndicated banks if commercial paper is issued or it could be on a funded basis if a revolving credit is drawn.
The facility guarantee fee is 62.5 basis points per annum if the facility is on an unfunded basis for the first three years.
If the revolving credit is drawn, the borrower will pay an interest margin of 110 basis points over three-month London Interbank Offered Rate.
The two-year bullet loan pays an interest margin of 95 basis points over the London Interbank Offered Rate.
Management fees are 40 basis points for lead managers committing US$10 million or above and 30 basis points for managers committing US$5-9 million.
Bankers Trust, Bank Indosuez, BNP, Commerz East Asia, Hamburgische Landesbank, IBJ, LTCB, Sanwa Bank, Sumitomo Bank and WestLB are underwriters and arrangers.
Bankers Trust, CS First Boston New York, Sanwa Bank and WestLB are coordinators. CS First Boston is the letter of credit issuing bank for the deal.
